Hi Diane / Sam,

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. To recap the items we discussed on audit logging and next steps for Acme:

- What we logged: admin activity (role changes, user provisioning, console actions), API request/response logs (timestamps, request metadata, request IDs), and system events (deploys, config changes).
- Exportability: logs are exportable via API and through CSV exports in the Console.
- Retention: default retention is 90 days on Hosted; Dedicated/Private options support configurable retention (30d–7yrs).
- Immutability: for Dedicated/Private we offer WORM (write-once, read-many) storage; Hosted provides append-only logs with tamper-evident checks and signed export bundles.

I've attached our SOC 2 Type II summary and a short audit-logging datasheet for your security team to review (full SOC 2 report available under NDA). If you want, we can also initiate your vendor security questionnaire — please attach it or let me know the preferred format.

Thanks, and great — I confirmed Tue 4/13 10:00 PT on the calendar (invite sent). Quick answers up front and attachments attached:

- SOC 2: Attached is the SOC 2 Type II summary and control matrix extract. We can provide the full auditor report under a standard NDA — I included a Drive link for the artifacts.
- GDPR/HIPAA: Redwood supports GDPR; we offer a standard DPA. For HIPAA, Redwood can support covered workloads under a Business Associate Agreement in Dedicated/Private deployments — we typically recommend Private for PHI workloads.
- Logs & export: Audit logs include admin activity (user/role changes, console actions), API request logs (headers, timestamps, request IDs, response codes), and system events. Exports are available as JSON or CSV via our Audit Export API and the Console export feature.
- Immutability: For Dedicated and Private we support WORM storage. On Hosted we provide append-only storage with tamper-evident checksums and signed export bundles (suitable for audit). If you need certified WORM for legal/regulatory reasons, we recommend Dedicated/Private.

Subject: Re: Audit logging discovery follow-up & next steps (technical details)

Hi Diane / Sam —

Thanks for looping me in. A few technical details ahead of tomorrow's call:

1) Endpoints:
- Audit export (bulk): POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/audit/logs/export
  - Accepts JSON filter (time range, event types, user ids) and returns a signed tarball with JSON lines + checksum file.
- Streaming/real-time: GET https://api.redwood.com/v1/audit/logs/stream (server-sent events) for live ingestion.

2) Export formats: NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) preferred for large exports, CSV available for smaller slices. Each event contains timestamp, request_id, actor_id, action, resource, metadata (IP, user-agent), and response_code where applicable.

3) Immutability / tamper evidence:
- Dedicated/Private: we enable WORM-backed object storage; writes are append-only and objects are versioned + retention-locked.
- Hosted: logs are stored append-only with SHA-256 checksums; exports are signed using our key and include a verification manifest. While Hosted provides tamper-evidence suitable for most audits, Dedicated/Private is the option for legally required WORM.

4) Retention & compliance options:
- Default Hosted retention: 90 days.
- Configurable in Dedicated: 30 days to 7 years.
- Export/archival: automated export to customer S3 buckets is supported for long-term archival.

5) Cryptographic proof: Signed export bundles include a PKCS7 signature and manifest with per-file checksums. We can provide the public key for verification or sign bundles under a customer-provided key in Dedicated deployments.

If you have specific fields your compliance team needs (e.g., full response bodies for certain endpoints), please flag them and we'll confirm retention/PII handling ahead of the call.

Looking forward to the call tomorrow — I'll demo an export and show verification steps.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
